title: AHB Accepted-Phase Core Checker
description: Step a transfer through visible, pending, accepted, data-owner, wait, ERROR, burst-count, alignment, and 1 KB state using configuration-derived legality checks.
learnerQuestion: Which AHB state advances on an accepted address or completed data phase, and which context must remain held?

configurations.label: AHB5 32-bit
configurations.description: Data width 4 bytes, RETRY/SPLIT illegal, every burst constrained to one 1 KB region.

configurations.label: Original AHB
configurations.description: AMBA 2 response set with RETRY/SPLIT enabled and shared-bus owner context.

scenarios.label: BUSY, wait, and reset state
scenarios.description: BUSY does not allocate a transfer, an ordinary wait retains the pending valid context, and reset flushes monitor and scoreboard state.

steps.label: Insert BUSY
steps.event: HREADY=1, HTRANS=BUSY inside an INCR burst

checks.label: BUSY is not a transfer
checks.evidence: Only NONSEQ/SEQ with HREADY HIGH allocate an accepted beat.

steps.label: Hold SEQ
steps.event: HREADY=0 with a pending SEQ address

checks.label: Pending beat remains unaccepted
checks.evidence: The wait extends the active data phase and freezes the pending valid address/control.

steps.label: Assert reset
steps.event: HRESETn asserts LOW during the wait

checks.label: Monitor state flushed
checks.evidence: Transfers active at reset are not required to complete; post-reset restart timing can be more conservative than the earliest legal edge.

checks.label: Scoreboard state flushed
checks.evidence: The environment cancels reset-aborted expectations consistently.

scenarios.label: Legal waited INCR4
scenarios.description: A wait freezes pending address/control and the active data phase; beat count advances only when the valid address is accepted.

checks.label: Accepted beat count
checks.evidence: NONSEQ with HREADY HIGH starts the burst.

checks.label: HSIZE within configured bus
checks.evidence: HSIZE cannot exceed the interface data width.

checks.label: Wait does not consume beat
checks.evidence: The pending SEQ address is visible but unaccepted.

checks.label: Complete pending context retained
checks.evidence: The pending valid address/control bundle remains stable during an ordinary wait.

checks.label: INCR4 exact count
checks.evidence: Only accepted NONSEQ/SEQ transfers contribute to the fixed-length burst.

checks.label: Final byte stays below 1 KB
checks.evidence: Every AHB burst remains within one 1 KB address region.

scenarios.label: Illegal 1 KB crossing
scenarios.description: A four-byte beat beginning at 0x400 belongs to a second 1 KB region and cannot continue the burst accepted below 0x400.

steps.label: Attempt crossing
steps.event: SEQ HADDR=0x400 after NONSEQ below boundary

checks.label: One 1 KB region
checks.evidence: The checker flags the address request; the manager must terminate and restart with NONSEQ before the boundary.

scenarios.label: Two-cycle ERROR
scenarios.description: Ordinary wait is OKAY; ERROR1 is not completion and ERROR2 completes the failed data phase.

checks.label: First ERROR cycle does not complete
checks.evidence: The master can cancel the pending address/control or retain it.

checks.label: Second ERROR cycle completes
checks.evidence: HREADY HIGH completes the failed data phase; post-error cancel/continue policy is checked separately.
